title: Canonical cotangent square, transitivity-arrow and scalar-extension constructions
statement: Fix standard polynomial cotangent coherence data $C$ [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data] and ordinary-module derived categories with localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a ring map $f:A\to B$, write $K_C(f)=s(\Omega^1_{P_C^{\mathrm{std}}/A}\otimes_{P_C^{\mathrm{std}}}B)$ for its recorded standard differential complex, and $L_C(f)=QK_C(f)$. For a commuting square $q=(a,b):f\to g$, write $\gamma_C(q):K_C(f)\to\operatorname{Res}_b K_C(g)$ for its recorded standard semilinear chain map. Ordinary scalar extension is $B'\otimes_B-$, with its tensor unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, right adjoint restriction, and termwise tensor/restriction adjunction on complexes [def-weil-module-base-change] [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{t}D$, define the first-term complex to be $D\otimes_B K_C(f)$, the first functoriality arrow to be $Q$ of the tensor adjunct of the standard square map $(\mathrm{id}_A,t):f\to tf$, and the second functoriality arrow $L_C(tf)\to L_C(t)$ to be $Q\gamma_C(f,\mathrm{id}_D)$ followed by the canonical identity-restriction identification. Let $F_b:D(B)\to D(B')$ be the existing universal left derived scalar-extension functor, computed using K-flat complexes [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], with its normalized derived adjunction to exact restriction, obtained from the ordinary tensor/restriction adjunction and the canonical exact-restriction comparison. Define the canonical cotangent square comparison $\beta_C(q):F_b(L_C(f))\to L_C(g)$ as the inverse derived Hom-equivalence applied to the recorded localized semilinear map $L_C(f)\to\operatorname{Res}_bL_C(g)$. These are constructions only: no vanishing, flatness, pushout, invertibility or distinguished-triangle assertion is part of this definition.
